title: ramp-limit-controller-and-utilization-auditor-for-dedicated-fleets
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce ramp limiter to bound autoscaler growth rate and a lightweight utilization auditor that periodically samples pod-level utilization and surfaces regressions to telemetry. Improves stability during bursty launches and reduces over-provisioning in steady state.
description:
Context: We observed two incidents where the Dedicated autoscaler reacted to short-lived spikes by provisioning large amounts of capacity, causing downstream allocation thrash (INC-2025-02) and higher costs for tenants. Root cause: lack of a controlled ramp when increasing desired replicas and limited short-window utilization sampling to verify demand. This PR introduces a ramp limit controller (RLC) that enforces a capped growth curve on reservation/slot allocations and a Utilization Auditor that provides sampled utilization percentiles to the autoscaler and operator dashboards.

Goals: 1) prevent >X% capacity jumps within a single control window without explicit operator override; 2) provide reliable short- and medium-window utilization measurements to detect noisy spikes vs sustained demand; 3) integrate with existing reservation and burst subsystems with minimal latency impact.

What this PR changes (summary):
- controller/rlc: new ramp_limit_controller.go implementing configurable growth_rate_pct, growth_window (s), and an override token check for emergency commits.
- auditor/util_auditor: new util_auditor.go and sampler that emits p50/p90/p99 utilization across tenants and per-queue short windows.
- api/types: added RampLimitConfig and UtilSample proto fields to ReservationSpec/Status for visibility and pinning.
- autoscaler/admission: updated admission path to consult ramp limiter before committing large reservation deltas; emits decision_trace to tracing.
- telemetry: new metrics (rlc_allowed_growth_pct, rlc_blocked_events_total, util_auditor_sample_count, util_auditor_latency_ms) and Grafana dashboard JSON snippet.
- e2e: new integration test harness that simulates bursty arrival patterns and asserts no >growth threshold within control windows.
- docs: architecture note and operator runbook describing override token usage and rollback steps.

Review conversation summary: 
- Wei: "Can you justify how growth_rate_pct was chosen?" -- Response: added rationale in docs and made the config adjustable by cluster-admins; default tuned to 25%/control-window after offline sim runs.
- Liam: Requested a safer default for retries and a short-circuit path for scheduled deployments; added override-token support and explicit audit log entries when used.
- Helena: Flagged that util sampling could add overhead; response: sampler is non-blocking, capped sample frequency, and we added a budgeted sampling mode in the auditor which falls back to headroom estimates if budget exhausted.
- Reviewer approvals: Wei (approved), Liam (approved after changes), Helena (requested one small test tweak which author addressed).

CI details:
- unit-tests: pass (ran in 3m)
- integration-tests: pass (flaky guard added, two simulated bursts validated)
- lint: pass
- e2e-staging: pass after one rerun (initial flakiness due to timing of the simulated load generator)

Deployment & rollout plan:
- feature gate: RampLimiter disabled by default in clusters older than v2025-02. Enable via cluster-config ramp_limiter.enabled=true for canary clusters.
- Monitoring: dashboards included; added alert rlc_blocked_events_rate > 5/min triggers on-call. The Utilization Auditor exports p90 and p99 that feed into the autoscaler's sustain detector.
- Rollback: remove feature gate or set growth_rate_pct to 100 to effectively disable ramping; short-circuit logs make rollback audits easy.

Testing notes:
- run `make test-integration -k TestRampLimitBurst` to reproduce harness scenario.
- metric names and dashboard references included in docs.

Related: ENG-4219 design doc, SUP-1124 customer report, and staging runbook (link to Linear and internal Confluence pages included in commit messages).

Post-merge follow-ups (tracked separately):
- Add tenant-level override policy and RBAC checks (ENG-4380).
- Calibrate default growth_rate_pct per-region based on historical burst histograms.

Why unique / risk: This approach trades off instantaneous elasticity for stability and cost predictability. We mitigated risk with audit logs, override tokens, and a phased rollout. The util auditor provides the empirical signal needed to avoid overly conservative defaults.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
